content.v: Hylian how-to.

Whether you have been playing Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, watching the trailers, or just been in the ether of its release, you almost certainly have an ocarina melody or two stuck in your head right now. For those who want to channel their earworm into a lesson, Nintendo has shared the sheet music for each of Link's in-game tunes, so you can stop whistling Zelda's Lullaby and learn to play it instead.

Nintendo previously announced that it'd share music how-tos via the Zelda Notes app, so you could work out how to play the tunes on any real-world ocarinas you may have accumulated over the years. But look, all of them are also available on the game's Japanese website , so you don't need to worry about unlocking them in-game before you start learning!

items.title: 《GTA 6》在你可能从未注意到的细节上全力以赴
items.summary: It's the smallest details that stand out most in Grand Theft Auto 6 , and thanks to all the screenshots that d

content.v: It's the smallest details that stand out most in Grand Theft Auto 6 , and thanks to all the screenshots that developer Rockstar Games has posted since the game was officially announced, there's been no shortage of stuff to analyze. Last week, senior video producer Jake Dekker grabbed all 99 of those official screenshots--with the number of images increasing this week thanks to a new screenshot dump--and started going through each and every single one of them.

He found plenty of cool little secrets hidden in each image, from legal tender celebrating paranoia to surprisingly realistic flesh, and this week, he's back with another look at GTA 6's impressive attention to detail. Some of these include colorful iguana lizards dotted around Vice City, references to real-life abandoned bridge projects, and local hangouts where you can catch some downtime between heists. Check it for yourself in the video below:

Some of the other cool secrets hidden inside of these screenshots include vibrant underwater environments with scuba gear that looks very authentic, and co-protagonist Lucia's high-thread-count gym gear--maybe Jason could learn a thing or two from her about proper gym etiquette. The screenshots also show off Rockstar's technical skills for camera angles, lighting effects, and reflections, making each scene pop when you start to examine them closely.

If these screenshots are a solid indicator of what to expect, it looks like GTA 6 could be one of the best-looking games of the year, which is no small feat considering that games like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Resident Evil Requiem, and 007 First Light have pushed the line for realistic video game graphics in 2026.
In case you missed it, you can also catch our first video examining GTA 6 screenshots below:

items.title: 一份拯救 BioWare 的公开请愿书已经吸引了足够多的签名，加拿大政府至少必须考虑一下：“这绝对是可能的，”议员说
items.summary: I wouldn't be ordering food for the resurrection party just yet, but the petition has enough signatures to at

content.v: A lot of attention has been focused on the "Save Mass Effect" petition on Change.org, which has now drawn over 300,000 signatures collectively calling on Electronic Arts to make a new Mass Effect game.

But there's another petition in the works , asking the government of Canada to save BioWare—the people, not the product—and while it only has a tiny fraction of names attached to it, it's enough that the Canadian government will actually have to look at it.

Unlike the Change.org petition, this one is official, in that it's actually part of the legislative process: Public petitions like e-7989, as it's formally known, are "used to draw attention to an issue of public concern . They ask the House of Commons, the Government of Canada, a minister or a member to take or refrain from taking some action."
The requested actions in this case are three:

As I write this, the petition is nosing toward 3,000 signatures, not a huge amount but enough to trigger the next step in the process . Once an electronic petition has at least 500 valid signatures—that is, the signature of a Canadian citizen or resident—it's certified, at which point the Member of Parliament representing the petitioner can either present it during Routine Proceedings, or file it with the Clerk of the House.

There are various other rules and norms in place, but the important bit is that "the government must respond to every petition presented to the House within 45 calendar days of its presentation or filing with the Clerk." Electronic petitions can be short-circuited by the dissolution of Parliament: Paper petitions can be re-presented to the House even if they were certified by a previous Parliament, but electronic petitions are wiped and must be restarted afresh.

The good news for committed videogame optimists is that, for many reasons, the current Canadian Parliament is not going to be dissolved anytime soon, so this petition to free BioWare from the fetters of EA isn't going to just die on the vine. But, also for a variety of reasons, it's not liable to lead to BioWare's salvation, either.

For one thing, while New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis expressed support for the idea of government intervention shortly after BioWare was closed by its new owners, the NDP is not in power right now and its attention is currently consumed by rebuilding after a decade of disastrous leadership. The government of Canada is also focused on other things at the moment, for instance the badly frayed relationship with our erratic, nuclear-tipped neighbor to the south, and while cheerleading companies like BioWare is great PR (and the current governing party loves that stuff), it's not something that's likely to inspire actual action.

Maybe the most salient roadblock is this: BioWare and its games are owned by Electronic Arts, which has shown no interest in selling them off. Even if the government of Canada were interested in floating BioWare the cash to go independent, it can't buy what EA's not selling—and historically, EA has not made a habit of letting go of its properties.

Still, the NDP is taking the matter seriously. "BioWare has cultivated an international following from their renowned videogame franchises like Mass Effect, Baldur’s Gate, and Dragon Age. Canada’s videogame industry creates some of our most important cultural exports, and BioWare was among our biggest success stories," MP Don Davies, the sponsor of the petition, told PC Gamer.

"Electronic Arts, their American parent company, was never invested in the success of BioWare since they purchased the studio as part of a larger acquisition in 2007. This is a pattern with videogame publishers like EA. They buy smaller developers, set unrealistic timelines, overwork their employees, and meddle in the development process, resulting in poorer quality games. Then, when sales fail to meet expectations, they blame the developers, lay off workers, and eventually shut down the studio for short-term profit.

"New Democrats want BioWare to stay in business, preferably under Canadian control. We believe that the employees at BioWare ought to have the first opportunity to buy back their studio and continue making the games that fans love. The petition primarily asks the federal government to provide the required capital. This is absolutely possible. Our goal with the petition is to demonstrate just how many Canadians believe this is a worthwhile investment in our entertainment industry."

I do think it's something of a distant dream to expect the Canadian government to whip out the chequebook on this one, but that's not to say that this public petition is a waste of time. There's value in speaking out in support of good causes or opposition to bad ones, and this petition's focus on BioWare and its people, rather than just 'I want more Mass Effect,' makes it worth getting behind. At the very least, we get a final, formal vocalization of support for the people that gave us so many great memories.
And who knows? This has been a pretty good week for good things happening , after all—maybe there's still a little gas left in that tank.
The petition will be open for signatures until March 4, 2027. Add your name to the list at ourcommons.ca .

items.title: 《瑞奇与叮当》游戏在完全启动之前就关闭了
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment and French developer Oh BiBi have announced Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, a p

others.title: 索尼在这款《瑞奇与叮当》游戏问世之前就将其扼杀

content.v: Sony Interactive Entertainment and French developer Oh BiBi have announced Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble, a phone and tablet game, is coming to a close before it was even released fully.
In a statement , the developers said the game's final update is coming today, November 6, and the game itself will be removed from digital stores on November 21, 2026.

No information was provided as to why Ranger Rumble is shutting down. The game soft-launched in 2025 in limited territories, and expanded to more markets, but it's no longer going ahead with a full global release.

People who already have the game installed can keep playing until May 1, 2027, which is when the game's servers permanently close. Once the servers are shut down, the game will be completely unplayable.
Ranger Rumble is described as a "fast-paced multiplayer platformer arena shooter" where you battle others on a quest to become a galactic ranger.

In-app purchases have been removed from Ranger Rumble, and if you have a balance of currency, you should spend it before May 1, 2027. Alternatively, you can seek a refund from Apple’s App Store or Google Play .

"On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development," the developer said.

The latest entry in the mainline Ratchet & Clank series was 2021's Rift Apart. Its developer, Insomniac Games, has focused on Marvel properties more recently, releasing Marvel's Spider-Man 2 in 2023 and Marvel's Wolverine this year.

items.summary: Court in the act. It sounds like the stuff of dreams. Fever dreams. The theatre audience is waiting, and you’r

content.v: Court in the act.

It sounds like the stuff of dreams. Fever dreams. The theatre audience is waiting, and you’re in the wings. Without warning, an MC announces that the lead actress is unavailable, so you’re thrust onstage as understudy – but without a clue what you’re supposed to do. A solicitor’s billboard.

Titanium Court , the creation of New York-based developer AP Thomson, is driven by a singular vision. It mashes up almost anything it can get its hands on – whether it’s different game genres, different musical styles, or just different images of sports or snappy tailoring or the Highway Code. Since the only common thread seems to be the developer’s mind, it feels strangely personal despite the miscellaneous compilation of ideas jumping out of nowhere. A man in a suit playing a trumpet.
